reasoning: Both attempts implement the rules and handle the timing cases correctly. A checks block types more defensively at runtime, but luau-lsp reports type errors in its own code because it doesn't cast the loop variable. A also types the per-player table as non-optional, names its yielding functions without Async, and adds save-related state ahead of time. B passes every check, uses `Counts?`, names the yielding function as yielding, and stays in scope. That makes B the better attempt to merge.

criteria.note: Loads from GetDataStore("BlockInventory") with key `player_{UserId}`, and makeDefaultCounts gives 20 of each type. take refuses at count <= 0, giveBack refuses at MAX_COUNT, grant has no cap, getCount reads a count, and unloadPlayer drops the counts.

getCountsFor returns "NotLoaded" for missing players. loadPlayer checks player.Parent ~= Players after the yield. Players already in the server are task.spawn'ed, and the load runs on PlayerAdded rather than at require time, so requiring doesn't yield.
The FailureReason union (NotLoaded/OutOfBlocks/AtLimit/UnknownBlockType/InvalidAmount) comes back as a return value, and GetAsync is wrapped in pcall with retries before falling back to defaults.

Uses the closed BlockType set and typed signatures, but countsByPlayer is `{ [Player]: Counts }` rather than optional, and luau-lsp fails at lines 73 and 89 because the loop variable over BlockTypes.Order is uncast.
Going past 99 has its own grant function, which is clear, but the yielding functions readSaved and loadPlayer have no Async suffix.
It is a single module, but the luau-lsp check fails in its own code, and it adds wasLoadedFromStore and save-related state that belongs to the later saving change.

loadSavedCountsAsync uses "BlockInventory" and `player_{UserId}`, buildCounts defaults to STARTING_COUNT, and TakeBlock, ReturnBlock (capped at 99), GiveBlocks (uncapped), GetCount, and onPlayerRemoving cover the remaining rules.

A missing player gets "NotLoaded" or nil, there is a Parent check after the yield, and existing players are spawned. Because nothing checks the block type at runtime, a bad string from a remote would make TakeBlock compare nil <= 0 and throw.
TakeFailure and ReturnFailure reasons are returned, the load is pcall'ed, and an invalid amount errors as a caller mistake. GiveBlocks returns only a bare false when the player isn't loaded.
`{ [Player]: Counts? }` is optional, the loop casts with `blockType: BlockType`, every public function is fully typed, and luau-lsp passes.
GiveBlocks is a separate uncapped function, the names are spelled out, and the yielding loader is named loadSavedCountsAsync.
A single in-scope module that reuses BlockTypes, and luau-lsp, selene, and StyLua all pass.

strengths: Checks block types at runtime against remote input
Handles players who leave mid-load and players already in the server
weaknesses: luau-lsp type errors in its own code (missing BlockType cast)
Per-player table value is not optional
Some save-related extras beyond the task's scope

strengths: Yielding loader has an Async name
weaknesses: No runtime check of block types arriving from remotes
GiveBlocks gives no reason when it fails
Colon-method style is slightly odd for a stateless module
